**Contextuality** — whether outcomes can be explained without reference to the context of measurement — Kochen–Specker and Bell contextuality and their sheaf-theoretic form, generalized (Spekkens) contextuality, noncontextual models and their limits, and contextuality outside physics.

| [THEORY-020](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-020.md) | KS obstruction lies in how contexts overlap | Stone (1936, 1937), [LIT-353](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-353.md) and [LIT-358](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-358.md): every Boolean ring is isomorphic to the compact open sets of its prime-ideal space, a totally disconnected, locally compact Hausdorff space that is compact exactly when there is a unit, and every such space arises this way. | [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Global sections restore classical Boolean logic | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |

| [THEORY-168](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-168.md) v4 | Contextuality depends on the representation | Dzhafarov, Cervantes & Kujala (2017), [LIT-790](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-790.md), with Dzhafarov & Kujala's CbD 2.0 ([LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md)) and CbD 1.0 ([LIT-777](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-777.md)). The same measurements can receive different verdicts. Maximal and multimaximal couplings can disagree when a content appears in three or more contexts (four, for binary variables), and the record's worked case shows it. Multimaximal couplings of non-binary variables can be destroyed by coarse-graining. With every dichotomization kept, two content-sharing variables are contextual on their own unless one nominally dominates the other. The authors present the representation as the analyst's choice, not as a defect. What the record does not get from these papers is any rule for choosing it. | Active |
| [THEORY-171](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-171.md) v5 | Causal structure is a source of contextuality | From Gogioso & Pinzani's trilogy: The Topology of Causality, [LIT-808](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-808.md), read in [NOTE-612](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-612.md), with the definitions of The Combinatorics of Causality, [LIT-800](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-800.md) ([NOTE-635](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-635.md)). Over a space of input histories with the lowerset topology, causal functions form a separated presheaf, and on the space Θ₃ it is not a sheaf: two causal assignments on disjoint opens give one event two outputs on their common extension. That example was checked here, and it settles the claim. The source's Theorem 2.34, that the presheaf is a sheaf exactly when no two contexts impose incompatible causal pasts on a common event, is reported as the source's. Its proof was not read, and it is QUESTION-143. It does not say any physical or quantum data display the effect. | Active |
| [THEORY-174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-174.md) v5 | Classical simulations never create contextuality | Karvonen (2018), [LIT-846](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-846.md); Abramsky, Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2019), [LIT-847](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-847.md); Barbosa, Karvonen & Mansfield (2021, v2 2024), [LIT-845](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-845.md). | [THEORY-403](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-403.md) | Classical toy field reproduces Mach–Zehnder | Catani, Leifer, Schmid & Spekkens (2021), [LIT-019](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-019.md), read in full in [NOTE-018](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-018.md). | [THEORY-474](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-474.md) | Toy-bit ZX calculus mirrors stabilizer theory | Backens & Duman (2014), [LIT-054](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-054.md), read in full in [NOTE-066](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-066.md). | [THEORY-722](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-722.md) | CbD 2.0 contextuality depends on representation | Dzhafarov & Kujala (2017), [LIT-831](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-831.md), Examples 1–3 and Section 4, read in [NOTE-643](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-643.md) (claims C4 and C6).
